# Stage report: release-notes

## Stage

2, draft, as an improvement. The template, its cases, a label and a round report exist, and the label is
`unsupported`.

## Request

> release-notes came out unsupported in its last round. The round report is evals/results/release-notes-round-2.md and the label is evals/results/release-notes.json. Fix the skill.

## Path

Improve the template that is there. Nothing is borrowed: its metadata says `sourcing: new`, so there is no source,
commit or licence to record.

The label names one gap: trigger accuracy 0.85 against the 0.9 floor. The task cases passed 6 of 6. The round
report names three train cases that should load the skill and missed in every run:

- `announce-whats-new`
- `release-page-list`
- `since-last-version`

All three ask for the write-up of what is new in a released version, for customers or for a release page. The old
description spoke only of a tagged version and its merged pull requests. So the description is the one line that
changed. It now names that intent, and its do-not-use part names the four train near misses: a changelog entry for
one pull request, a commit message, a blog post about the team and a migration guide. No prompt of a case is in
it. The name, licence, metadata and steps 1 to 3 are as they were. `v2/VERSION` went from 0.4.1 to 0.4.2.

- `wc -l` gives 17 lines for the template and 1 for `v2/VERSION`.
- The new description against the three prompts in the round report, read side by side: it shares no run of five

- The test split: the round report does not name its cases, and none was read.

  commit `b21f9aa`, version 0.4.1) and no skill.
- Whoever holds the build: run `python3 v2/build/build.py` and report what it prints.
